blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
blueprint.competency_task: Identifies the cellular transport defect producing renal Fanconi syndrome.

difficulty.rationale: Requires integration of discriminating clinical clues with a mechanism or diagnosis rather than isolated fact recall.

option_audit.correct: Explains the CTNS/cystinosin molecular defect and all renal plus ocular findings.
option_audit.cystinuria: Shares cystine terminology but causes urinary cystine loss/stones rather than lysosomal storage/Fanconi syndrome.
option_audit.OCRL: Can produce proximal tubular dysfunction but not corneal cystine deposition from CTNS deficiency.
option_audit.FGF23: Produces selective phosphate wasting rather than generalized proximal tubular solute loss.
option_audit.tenofovir: Can cause acquired Fanconi syndrome but is incompatible with the inherited infantile ocular-storage phenotype.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Infantile growth failure, polyuria/polydipsia, generalized proximal tubular wasting, rickets and corneal cystine crystals identify nephropathic cystinosis; CTNS loss removes cystinosin-mediated lysosomal cystine export.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Cystinuria also involves cystine transport but is an apical renal amino-acid transport defect causing urinary cystine stones, not intracellular lysosomal storage, corneal crystals, or generalized Fanconi syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.other_distractors: OCRL/Lowe syndrome can cause Fanconi physiology, FGF23 excess can cause phosphate wasting/rickets, and tenofovir can cause acquired proximal tubular injury; none explains the complete multisystem cystinosis pattern.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: The corneal crystals are a legitimate discriminating clue; the answer still requires linking the syndrome to the lysosomal transporter and direction of cystine movement.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No unsupported prevalence, numeric cystine threshold, drug dose, or age cutoff is asserted.
